title: Prawns in Garlic Cream Broth
subtitle: King prawns in a white wine style cream and herb broth
excerpt: Shell-on king prawns cooked in a fragrant broth of onion, garlic, thyme, cream, and parsley in the style of moules mariniere. Traditional moules mariniere uses mussels; this version uses king prawns for a dish that is equally quick and suited to the same bowl-and-bread treatment.
sourceNotes: Moules mariniere is a classic of French and Belgian coastal cooking, traditionally made by steaming mussels with white wine, shallots, and herbs. The dish dates to at least the 19th century and is closely associated with the cooking of Normandy and Brittany. This prawn version applies the same method to shell-on king prawns.

content.text: Shell-on prawns give far more flavour to the broth than peeled ones. Provide fingerbowls or plenty of napkins and crusty bread for mopping up the sauce.
Melt the butter in the stockpot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute.
Add the thyme, bay leaves, and 150 ml of water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the prawns, cover with a lid, and cook over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until the prawns are pink and cooked through.
Pour in the cream and stir gently. Cook for 1 minute to warm through. Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir in the parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Serve in deep bowls with lemon wedges and crusty bread.

items.fix: Watch closely and remove from heat as soon as prawns are pink.

items.cause: Not enough reduction before cream was added
items.fix: Simmer the broth for 3 to 4 minutes before adding cream.

items.cause: Cream was added to a boiling sauce
items.fix: Reduce heat before adding cream and stir gently.
